title: RBI Draft Aligns Leverage Ratio Regime with Basel 2017 Standards; Prescribes G-SIB Leverage Buffer
summary: RBI draft directions align leverage ratio norms with Basel 2017, introducing leverage buffer for G-SIB (global systemically important bank capital surcharge) branches in India from April 1, 2027.

blocks.title: 📰 2. 🏛️ REGULATORY BODIES NEWS
blocks.text: 🪝 RBI Draft Aligns Leverage Ratio Regime with Basel 2017 Standards; Prescribes G-SIB Leverage Buffer. Key development for Banking & General Awareness.

items: RBI draft directions align leverage ratio norms with Basel 2017, introducing leverage buffer for G-SIB (global systemically important bank capital surcharge) branches in India from April 1, 2027.
**Minimum Leverage Ratio:** Retained at **4% for D-SIBs** and **3.5% for all other banks**.

**G-SIB (global systemically important bank capital surcharge) Branches:** Foreign branches of G-SIBs must maintain **3.5% minimum leverage ratio + applicable G-SIB (global systemically important bank capital surcharge) leverage buffer**.
**Derivative Calculation:** Uses replacement cost + potential future exposure, multiplier generally **1.4x**.
≠ **Ratio Floor:** D-SIBs floor is 4.0%; Non-D-SIB commercial banks floor is 3.5%.
🎯 Exam Angle → Focus on statutory circular guidelines, compliance deadlines, penal provisions, and applicability thresholds across scheduled banks.
